Introduction to Geisinger

The California Health Care Foundation released a report in January 2022 that looked at hospitalizations and treatment episodes related to alcohol and drugs. This report showed that individuals between the ages of 18 and 25 had a higher prevalence of substance use disorders, with a higher rate for alcohol use disorders followed closely by illicit drugs.

A positive finding of this report is that there was an increase of individuals who sought treatment in an outpatient treatment facility, residential inpatient facility, and a hospital inpatient program in 2019 when compared to previous years.

Does Geisinger Insurance Cover Substance Abuse Treatment?

Geisinger Insurance does cover substance abuse treatment for its members. When we look at inpatient treatment services, Geisinger can provide coverage for members who struggle with the use of alcohol, opioid, sedative, and stimulants. Additionally, you are eligible for medication-assisted treatment (MAT), treatment programs for uniform professionals, and treatment programs for healthcare professionals.

When we look at the outpatient treatment options available for Geisinger insurance members are eligible for medication-assisted treatment (MAT), minor withdrawal management, group therapy, individual therapy, and peer support groups. Additionally, Geisinger members are eligible for consultations and assessments for individuals with a history of addiction and those with a history of pain and addiction.

How Long Will Geisinger Insurance Cover Drug Detox?

The length of time that Geisinger will provide for coverage depends on a variety of factors. This includes the severity of your addiction, the recommendation from a treatment provider, the presence of medical health concerns, and the presence of mental health concerns. Some individuals may find that all of their treatment is covered, while others may have some of the cost fall onto them.

With the individual differences within Geisinger’s healthcare plans, it is important to understand that there may be individual differences within your plan’s coverage when compared to other members. This can influence your deductible and co-pays.
